submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 has the highest efficiency of the three candidates at every threshold scanned. Its best scanned efficiency is about 92.4% at 37 GeV, against 85.1% for the runner-up L3. Repeat measurements (30 GeV: 91.8 and 89.8; 40 GeV: 91.1 and 90.9) show about 1–2% scatter. So the efficiency curve is flat from roughly 30 to 40 GeV, and the choice of 37 GeV is within noise. The L1 lead of about 7 points is well outside that scatter. 37 GeV lies in the allowed 20–60 GeV range. The efficiencies were measured at the allocated 8 kHz rate, but I did not confirm that the rate at 37 GeV stays within 8 kHz. The latency budget is undocumented and latency has not been verified for any candidate, so L1 deployability is only partly confirmed. This should be checked before the algorithm is deployed.

requirements.requirement: Highest possible signal efficiency at allocated rate (8 kHz)
requirements.evidence: L1 reaches 92.437% at 37 GeV, versus 85.131% for L3 and 73.656% for L2. The plateau noise is about 1%, so the exact threshold is not significant. I did not confirm that the rate at 37 GeV is within 8 kHz.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates

requirements.evidence: The deployable flag is 1, FPGA resources fit and link bandwidth is OK. The latency budget is undocumented and latency_verified=0 for all candidates.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold
requirements.evidence: This submission recommends Algorithm-L1 at 37 GeV.
